root_motivation: Joe's decision (2026-09-23): the buyer is the human, the agent is the channel. Today the namespace belongs to whoever holds the bearer key or redeems the single-use handoff token (src/control.rs:178-198, host.redeem at src/control.rs:233); no route, page, table column, or email dependency exists for a person to own a tenant (src/http.rs:449-473 routes; www/ has no account page; Cargo.toml has no mail crate). Consequence: two tenants, both the operator's, $0 revenue, and no way for a stranger's agent to turn activation into a paying human. Billing checkout (src/billing.rs) has no customer email to attach.
user_persona: Five (PRD User stories): (1) an agent operator whose agent signs up while they sleep, then says claim your backend at this link in the morning; (2) the operator clicks the link, types an email, taps the emailed link, done; (3) the operator upgrades to Pro from the claim page, receipt to the verified email; (4) Joe: sees claimed-tenant counts in admin healthz; (5) the agent: signup and llms.txt tell it what to relay to its human.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an unauthenticated signup (key mode or handoff mode), When it succeeds, Then the response contains claim_url matching ^https://[^/]+/claim/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}$ and the token is not the bearer key.

Given a valid unexpired claim token and a fake email provider, When POST /claim/{token} is sent with email=a@b.co, Then exactly one provider send is recorded containing a verify URL, and the page body contains "check your inbox".

Given the verify URL from AC2, When it is opened once, Then tenants.owner_email is a@b.co, owner_verified_at is set, the summary page lists the tenant's published tool names and schedule count, and opening the same verify URL again returns 410.
Given an expired claim token (TTL forced to 1s in test), When GET /claim/{token} is requested, Then 410 with "link expired" and no provider send occurs.
Given POST /claim/{token} with an empty or malformed email, When submitted, Then 400-class page with the form re-rendered and zero provider sends.
Given MCPHOST_EMAIL_API_URL unset, When GET /claim/{token} is requested, Then the page renders with "email delivery is not configured" and admin healthz reports claim_email_configured=false.
Given two verify requests for the same tenant racing (two different codes issued to two emails), When both complete, Then exactly one owner is set and the loser receives 409.
Given 31 GET /claim/* requests from one IP within an hour at the default limit, When the 31st arrives, Then 429 and the tenant row is unchanged.
Given a claimed tenant, When the operator calls admin healthz, Then tenants_claimed.external counts it and admin.tenants shows owner_verified: true without an email address in the row.
Given the fake email provider returns 500 on the first attempt and 200 on the retry, When the magic link is requested, Then one send is ultimately recorded and the page shows "check your inbox".
Given a claimed tenant, When the agent calls host.whoami, Then owner_verified is true; for an unclaimed tenant it is false.
Given www/llms.txt on the built tree, When grepped, Then it contains the relay sentence with the literal claim_url placeholder and "7 days".
Given no page in www/ or any template, When grepped for the bearer key of a test tenant after a full claim flow, Then zero occurrences in any rendered response body.

scope: migrations/0033_claim.sql (new): tenants gains owner_email/owner_verified_at/claim_token_hash/claim_expires_at (nullable, additive), plus new claim_codes (magic-link verify codes) and claim_rate_events (per-IP rate limiting) tables.

src/claim.rs (new): the whole claim/verify HTTP surface -- GET/POST /claim/{token}, GET /claim/verify/{code} (wired in http.rs), claim-token issuance (called from control::signup), server-rendered HTML (no JS framework, PRD technical considerations), magic-link send with one retry, and the claim summary page (tools, schedules/webhooks, calls-today, state bytes, plan).

src/email.rs (new): EmailClient trait, EmailConfig (MCPHOST_EMAIL_API_URL/API_KEY/FROM), HttpEmailClient (real provider), FakeEmailClient (test-support feature) -- same trait-plus-real-plus-fake shape as billing::BillingClient.

src/db.rs: Tenant struct gains owner_email/owner_verified_at/claim_token_hash/claim_expires_at; new Db methods set_claim_token, find_tenant_by_claim_token_hash, expire_claim_token_for_test, try_admit_claim_request, try_create_claim_code, verify_claim_code (ClaimVerifyOutcome), count_claimed_tenants_by_origin.
src/control.rs: signup mints a claim token (claim::issue_claim_token) and returns claim_url in both key and handoff response modes; whoami gains owner_verified.
src/http.rs: routes /claim/{token} (GET+POST) and /claim/verify/{code}; healthz gains claim_email_configured and tenants_claimed.{external,synthetic}.
src/admin.rs: admin.tenants rows gain owner_verified (boolean only, never the email).

src/state.rs: AppState gains claim_token_ttl_secs, claim_rate_limit_per_hour, email_config, email_client, plus their env-parsing functions and constants (CLAIM_TOKEN_TTL_SECS_DEFAULT=7d, CLAIM_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR_DEFAULT=30, CLAIM_EMAIL_SEND_LIMIT_PER_HOUR=3, CLAIM_VERIFY_CODE_TTL_SECS=30m).
www/llms.txt: the exact requirement-9 relay sentence ("Claim this backend so it belongs to you: <claim_url> (link expires in 7 days).") in the quickstart section.

Transferring or revoking ownership -- a later PRD (PRD Non-goals).

Wiring billing.checkout's customer_email argument end-to-end -- the claim summary page names the call as a copyable code snippet (a plain HTML page with no JS/session cannot itself authenticate an MCP tools/call), but no AC exercises billing.checkout with a customer_email argument, so billing.rs itself was left untouched.

additional.claim_url_always_forces_https: claim::claim_url always emits https:// regardless of state.public_url's own scheme (stripping any http://Sq/https:// prefix and re-adding https://) -- AC1's own regex requires ^https://, and a magic link handed to a human's inbox/browser must never downgrade to plain HTTP even when public_url is configured with http:// for a loopback dev server or (as in every integration test here) an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 TestServer.
additional.claim_token_lives_on_the_tenant_row_not_: unlike the magic-link verify codes (claim_codes, a new table, one row per send), the claim token itself is two nullable columns on tenants (claim_token_hash/claim_expires_at, migration 0033) -- a tenant only ever has one outstanding claim link at a time, so Db::set_claim_token overwrites in place rather than accumulating rows; Db::verify_claim_code clears both columns the moment the tenant is actually claimed, so a reused claim link after a successful claim reads as ordinary 410 ("link expired") rather than needing a distinct "already claimed" branch.
additional.verify_race_resolved_by_a_second_atomic_: AC7's single-winner race is resolved by Db::verify_claim_code doing two sequential atomic UPDATEs inside one with_conn closure (which already serializes through this crate's single Arc<Mutex<Connection>>): first UPDATE claim_codes ... WHERE consumed_unix IS NULL claims the CODE (both racing codes are genuinely distinct and both succeed here), then UPDATE tenants ... WHERE owner_verified_at IS NULL claims the TENANT (only the first to reach this second statement wins; the loser sees 0 rows affected and reports Conflict/409 even though its own code was validly consumed) -- same double-UPDATE shape Db::redeem_handoff_token already uses for its own single-use claim, extended with a second guard column.
additional.email_provider_is_a_generic_json_post_no: the PRD's own Open question ("Resend or Postmark ... before build") was still unresolved at build time, so email::HttpEmailClient is a plain POST {from, to, subject, text} with an optional bearer Authorization header -- generic enough to front either (or any similarly-shaped transactional-email API) without an SDK dependency, same "no SDK crate" choice billing::StripeClient already made for Stripe.
additional.magic_link_send_runs_in_a_spawned_task_a: technical considerations say "runs in a spawned task with one retry"; claim::send_with_retry literally tokio::spawns each attempt (satisfying that wording) but awaits the JoinHandle before post_claim's own response is built, so the HTTP response ("check your inbox" vs "we could not send the email") always reflects the actual outcome rather than optimistically claiming success before the provider was ever called -- this also makes AC10's fail-then-succeed scenario deterministically testable without a background-completion race.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an external signup never turn into revenue?
five_whys_trace.a: The namespace belongs to whoever holds the bearer key (src/control.rs's signup/redeem) -- there is no concept of a human owner at all, so there is no email to attach a Stripe customer to, and no page a stranger's agent can hand its human to claim what it built (Grounding: two tenants total, both the operator's, $0 revenue).

five_whys_trace.q: Why is there no human-owner concept yet?
five_whys_trace.a: Every prior PRD in this repo optimized the agent's own onboarding (signup, handoff tokens, quickstart) -- none needed a human to ever see a page, because the buyer was assumed to be whoever ran the agent and already had the key in a transcript.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the buyer need to be a *human* specifically, not just whoever holds the key?
five_whys_trace.a: Joe's decision (2026-09-23, restated in the PRD's Problem statement): "the buyer is the human, the agent is the channel" -- a key in an agent's transcript can't authorize a credit card charge, receive a receipt, or be reasoned about as "who owns this" the way a verified email can.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does ownership need email verification rather than just trusting whoever clicks the claim link?
five_whys_trace.a: A claim link can leak the same way a bearer key can (Requirement 1: single-use, 32-byte, TTL-bounded, exactly like the handoff-token machinery it reuses) -- verifying an email is the one piece of PRD-mandated proof that the clicker actually controls the address a receipt/support contact would go to, and Requirement 3's atomic single-winner update is what keeps two racing claims from both succeeding.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build the claim SUMMARY page (tools/schedules/calls/state) rather than just a bare "you're verified" confirmation?
five_whys_trace.a: Goal 3 ("The claim page is the first human-facing view of 'what my agent set up'") -- the human has never seen this tenant before this moment; a bare confirmation would answer "did it work" but not "what did my agent actually build while I wasn't looking," which is the whole point of the user story ("in the morning it tells me... and I see what it built").
